title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
title_zh: 自蒸馏未来视频表示用于世界动作模型

paragraphs.en: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce F uture RE presentation learning via self- D istillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step. Specifically, FRED uses self-distillation to predict future representations from noise, using representations extracted from ground-truth future observations as targets. We further condition the video model on historical observations, providing temporal context for predicting future representations better. Across diverse real-world manipulation scenarios, FRED consistently outperforms competing WAMs. It achieves particularly large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks under zero-shot environment generalization, and substantially improves human-to-robot skill transfer, reaching 50.0% task success on tasks absent from robot training data and demonstrated only in human videos, compared with 19.4% for the best competing WAM.

paragraphs.en: World Action Models (WAMs; Pai et al. 2025 ; Liang et al. 2025 ; Kim et al. 2026b ; Ye et al. 2026 ) have recently emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies. Built on pre-trained video diffusion models (VDMs; Wan et al. 2025 ; Ali et al. 2025 ), WAMs have shown strong generalization to unseen tasks ( Ye et al., 2026 ; Ma et al., 2026 ) , adaptation to new robot embodiments ( Ye et al., 2026 ) , and skill transfer from human videos to robots ( Dyna Robotics, 2026 ) . Their core idea is to leverage the rich spatiotemporal priors learned from large-scale in-the-wild video datasets ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Nan et al., 2024 ) by training a model to jointly predict future frames and corresponding actions. This allows the strong generalization capabilities of pre-trained video models to extend from future video prediction to robot control.

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we aim to improve the control performance of the recent line of WAMs that use a single VDM forward pass for action generation. We start by performing an analysis of how well the VDM hidden states learn meaningful information to generate actions during WAM training. We first find that VDM hidden states generated from noise already capture information about future robot motion. Specifically, a lightweight probe trained on frozen hidden states can predict future motion primitives, with classification accuracy increasing throughout WAM training (see Figure 1(a) ). Moreover, these hidden states become increasingly similar to those extracted from ground-truth future observations at the same VDM layer (see Figure 1(b) ). These findings suggest that the VDM progressively learns to generate future video representations from noise. However, a clear gap in future-motion probing accuracy remains relative to representations extracted from clean future observations, suggesting that generating sufficiently informative future representations from noise remains challenging.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们旨在提升近期一系列使用单次 VDM 前向传播生成动作的 WAM 的控制性能。 我们首先分析了在 WAM 训练过程中，VDM 隐状态在多大程度上学习了有意义的信息以生成动作。 我们首先发现，由噪声生成的 VDM 隐状态已经能够捕获关于未来机器人运动的信息。 具体而言，在冻结的隐状态上训练的轻量级探针可以预测未来的运动基元，其分类准确率在 WAM 训练过程中持续提升（见图 1(a)）。 此外，这些隐状态在相同 VDM 层上与从真值未来观测中提取的表示越来越相似（见图 1(b)）。 这些发现表明，VDM 逐步学会从噪声中生成未来的视频表示。 然而，相对于从干净未来观测中提取的表示，未来运动探测准确率仍存在明显差距，这表明从噪声中生成足够富含信息的未来表示仍然具有挑战性。

paragraphs.en: Inspired by this, we propose F uture RE presentation learning via self- D istillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework for training WAMs to improve the future representations obtained from a single video denoising step for action generation; see the overview in Figure 2 . We train the VDM through self-distillation to align representations generated from noise with those extracted from ground-truth future observations, encouraging the model to capture richer future information for predicting actions. Specifically, FRED uses a momentum teacher, implemented as an Exponential-Moving-Average (EMA) copy of the online VDM, to extract the target representations from noisy future observations at the same intermediate layer used for action conditioning. We further condition the VDM on a short history of observations, providing temporal context that helps the intermediate hidden states better represent future robot motion. As a result, FRED reduces the future-motion probing performance gap to representations extracted from clean future observations and further improves structural similarity to them (see Figure 1 ). Notably, this closer alignment with representations of future observations translates into better robot control performance (see Figure 4(c) ).
paragraphs.zh: 受此启发，我们提出了 FRED（通过带时间上下文的自蒸馏进行未来表征学习），这是一个用于训练世界动作模型（WAM）的框架，旨在改进单步视频去噪所获得的用于动作生成的未来表征；概述见图 2。 我们通过自蒸馏训练 VDM，使从噪声中生成的表征与从真实未来观测中提取的表征对齐，从而促使模型捕获更丰富的未来信息以预测动作。 具体而言，FRED 使用一个动量教师，即在线 VDM 的指数移动平均（EMA）副本，在用于动作条件化的同一中间层上从含噪未来观测中提取目标表征。 我们进一步以一段较短的观测历史作为 VDM 的条件，提供时间上下文，帮助中间隐状态更好地表征未来机器人运动。 因此，FRED 缩小了未来运动探测性能与从干净未来观测中提取的表征之间的差距，并进一步提升了与它们在结构上的相似性（见图 1）。 值得注意的是，这种与未来观测表征的更紧密对齐转化为更好的机器人控制性能（见图 4(c)）。

paragraphs.en: To validate the generality and effectiveness of FRED, we conduct extensive experiments in diverse real-world robotic manipulation scenarios. We first evaluate FRED on zero-shot environment generalization using a varied set of real-world manipulation tasks, including long-horizon manipulation, out-of-domain tasks, and object grounding. Our results show that FRED consistently outperforms competing WAMs in these settings, improving long-horizon performance from 61.7% to 81.7% and out-of-domain task success from 10.4% to 52.1% at the 14B scale. We further evaluate FRED on human-to-robot skill transfer by co-training the video model on human videos without action labels, including tasks absent from robot training data. We show that FRED significantly outperforms competing WAMs, improving task success from 19.4% to 50.0%, while achieving 97.2% instruction-following performance. These results highlight that FRED improves future representation quality and achieves strong robot control in both zero-shot generalization and human-to-robot transfer.
paragraphs.zh: 为了验证 FRED 的通用性和有效性，我们在多样化的真实世界机器人操作场景中进行了大量实验。 我们首先使用一组多样化的真实世界操作任务评估 FRED 的零样本环境泛化能力，包括长时程操作、域外任务和物体定位。 结果表明，FRED 在这些设置中始终优于竞争的 WAM，在 14B 规模下将长时程性能从 61.7% 提升至 81.7%，将域外任务成功率从 10.4% 提升至 52.1%。 我们进一步通过在没有动作标签的人类视频上共同训练视频模型来评估 FRED 的人类到机器人技能迁移能力，其中包括机器人训练数据中不存在的任务。 我们表明，FRED 显著优于竞争的 WAM，将任务成功率从 19.4% 提升至 50.0%，同时实现了 97.2% 的指令遵循性能。 这些结果凸显了 FRED 提升了未来表征质量，并在零样本泛化和人类到机器人迁移两方面都实现了强大的机器人控制。

paragraphs.en: We interpret the VDM in WAMs as a future representation generator that produces intermediate hidden states containing predictive information about future robot motion in a single forward pass.

paragraphs.en: We present FRED, a framework that improves future video representations generated from noise for action prediction through self-distillation using representations extracted from ground-truth future observations as targets, and short-history conditioning for richer temporal context.

paragraphs.en: We show that FRED consistently outperforms baseline WAMs across diverse real-world manipulation settings: zero-shot environment generalization and human-to-robot skill transfer.

paragraphs.en: World Action Models. Prior work studies robot control via World Action Models (WAMs), which build on pre-trained video diffusion models (VDMs) and jointly model future observations and actions using robot data, allowing spatiotemporal priors from large-scale video to guide action generation ( Shen et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026a ; Kim et al., 2026b ; Ye et al., 2026 ) . These models generate plausible future visual states to support action prediction, but iterative denoising with large video backbones incurs substantial computational cost at inference time. Recent WAMs address this bottleneck by decoupling video and action generation and reducing video denoising to a single step. Within this shared design, some works predict actions without explicitly generating future videos at inference by masking access to future video features ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) or directly decoding actions from video-backbone states ( Li et al., 2026b ) . In contrast, another line of work conditions action prediction on future video representations obtained from noise in a single video denoising step ( Pai et al., 2025 ; Ma et al., 2026 ; Qiu et al., 2026 ; Zhao et al., 2026 ) . Our work follows the latter design and focuses on how to train WAMs to generate more informative future representations for action generation.

paragraphs.en: Diffusion Models and Representation Learning. Prior works have shown that diffusion denoisers learn discriminative representations useful for visual recognition ( Xiang et al., 2023 ; Yang & Wang, 2023 ; Li et al., 2023 ) . More recent work improves these representations during generative training, where REPA ( Yu et al., 2025 ) aligns noisy diffusion features with clean image representations from a pre-trained visual encoder, while SRA ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) uses lower-noise representations from the diffusion model itself as targets. This direction has been extended to VDMs through alignment with pre-trained video representations ( Zhang et al., 2026 ; Lee et al., 2025 ; Bhowmik et al., 2026 ) , while Self-Flow ( Chefer et al., 2026 ) incorporates self-supervised representation learning directly into flow matching without an external encoder. Our work studies representation learning in WAMs, where intermediate video representations from a single denoising step directly condition action generation. AGRA ( Qiu et al., 2026 ) adapts representation alignment to this setting by aligning these representations with features from a frozen visual encoder. FRED instead uses representations extracted from observed future frames as distillation targets for representations generated from noise. This improves the future video representation used by the action decoder without aligning the intermediate video features to a fixed external representation.

paragraphs.en: Implementation Details. We consider two different model scales for our experiments: 5B and 14B. For the 5B-scale experiments, we use Wan2.2-TI2V-5B ( Wan et al., 2025 ) as the video diffusion backbone and a 16-layer DiT ( Peebles & Xie, 2023 ) as the action decoder. For self-distillation in FRED, we extract features from 19th layer (index 18) of the video backbone for both the student and teacher, fix the teacher’s noise level at 0.25, and use λ SD = 0.01 \lambda_{\mathrm{SD}}=0.01 by default. We update the momentum teacher using an exponential moving average (EMA) of the student, with the decay warmed up using an inverse decay schedule. We use 4 historical observations with the current observation as input. For our 14B-scale experiments, we utilize the Wan2.1-I2V-14B ( Wan et al., 2025 ) with a 24-layer DiT action decoder and extract features from 25th layer of the video backbone for self-distillation. Unless otherwise stated, we extract video features from the same layer for self-distillation and action decoder conditioning. See more details in Appendix A .

paragraphs.en: Baselines. We use several recent robot foundation models as baselines. Results. As shown in Table 1 , we find that FRED consistently outperforms the other WAM baselines across all task types in the 5B video backbone setup. The improvements are particularly large on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks: compared with the strongest competing WAM baseline, FRED improves performance from 31.7% → \to 46.7% and from 10.4% → \to 37.5%, respectively, while also improving object grounding from 33.3% → \to 37.5%. paragraphs.en: Human Skill Transfer Results. In Table 2(b) , we observe that FRED achieves strong human-to-robot skill transfer when co-trained with human videos, while other WAM baselines show limited transfer on tasks demonstrated only in the human-video dataset. For example, DreamZero ( Ye et al., 2026 ) and AGRA ( Qiu et al., 2026 ) achieve instruction-following rates of only 13.9% and 0.0%, respectively, with zero task success for both, whereas FRED achieves an instruction-following rate of 97.2% and a task success rate of 50.0%. Notably, FRED reliably follows the target skills demonstrated in human videos, whereas most baseline WAMs, except DiT4DiT ( Ma et al., 2026 ) , often execute behaviors seen in the robot training tasks instead. Without human-video co-training, FRED and the baselines achieve near-zero task success. The VLA baselines nevertheless show some instruction-following behavior, possibly due to knowledge acquired during VLA pre-training. These results highlight the effectiveness of FRED in transferring skills from human videos to robot control, suggesting that future prediction in VDMs provides useful motion information for transfer and that explicitly learning future video representations independently of robot action optimization may further improve human-to-robot transfer.

paragraphs.en: Comparison with Representation Learning Methods. To verify the effectiveness of FRED as a representation learning method for WAMs, we compare FRED with recent representation learning approaches for diffusion models, i . e ., VideoREPA ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , SRA ( Jiang et al., 2025 ) , and Self-Flow ( Chefer et al., 2026 ) , on RoboCasa Kitchen ( Nasiriany et al., 2024 ) , GR-1 Tabletop ( Bjorck et al., 2025 ) , and LIBERO ( Liu et al., 2023 ) benchmarks. In Table 4 , VideoREPA, SRA, and Self-Flow generally show modest gains over the base WAM, whereas FRED achieves consistently larger improvements across all benchmarks. This suggests that directly learning the future representations generated from noise is particularly effective for improving action control in WAMs.

paragraphs.en: Future Representation Quality and Robot Control. Since the action decoder directly conditions on future video representations generated from noise, their quality may be closely correlated with robot control performance. To investigate this, we use DiT4DiT ( Ma et al., 2026 ) as the base WAM and compare variants with different VDM training objectives along these three dimensions: one-step video generation quality, representation quality on observed future videos, and the quality of future representations generated from noise. Specifically, the WAM variants include an objective that explicitly improves one-step video generation through step-distillation (DMD2; Yin et al. 2024 ) and representation learning objectives that improve intermediate video representations. We measure video generation quality using Fréchet Video Distance (FVD; Unterthiner et al. 2018 ). For the representation quality, we follow prior works on evaluating visual representation with frozen-backbone probing ( Yu et al., 2025 ; Assran et al., 2025 ) . In particular, we train a lightweight attentive probe on the video representations to classify each video into predefined motion primitive classes (see Appendix D for more detailed setup).
paragraphs.zh: 未来表征质量与机器人控制。 由于动作解码器直接以从噪声生成的未来视频表征为条件，其质量可能与机器人控制性能密切相关。 为研究这一点，我们使用 DiT4DiT（Ma et al., 2026）作为基础 WAM，并沿以下三个维度比较采用不同 VDM 训练目标的变体：单步视频生成质量、在观测到的未来视频上的表征质量，以及从噪声生成的未来表征的质量。 具体而言，WAM 变体包括一个通过步蒸馏显式提升单步视频生成的目标（DMD2；Yin et al. 2024），以及改进中间视频表征的表征学习目标。 我们使用 Fréchet 视频距离（FVD；Unterthiner et al. 2018）来衡量视频生成质量。 对于表征质量，我们遵循先前使用冻结主干探测来评估视觉表征的工作（Yu et al., 2025；Assran et al., 2025）。 特别地，我们在视频表征上训练一个轻量级的注意力探测头，将每个视频分类到预定义的运动基元类别中（更详细的设置见附录 D）。

paragraphs.en: Self-distillation Design Choices. We analyze several design choices of FRED: teacher noise level, feature extraction layer used for both self-distillation and action conditioning, self-distillation loss coefficient, and gradient flow from the action loss to the video diffusion backbone. In Table 5(a) , we find that a moderately noisy teacher input with τ = 0.25 \tau=0.25 performs best, outperforming both clean future observations and more heavily corrupted inputs. We hypothesize that moderate corruption provides more informative target representations for self-distillation, consistent with prior observations that representations from diffusion models can be strongest at intermediate noise levels ( Yu et al., 2025 ; Vélez et al., 2025 ) . In Table 5(b) , we find that performance peaks at layer index 18, while using either shallower or deeper layers degrades performance, which aligns with prior findings in WAMs that intermediate video-model layers provide more effective representations for action conditioning ( Ma et al., 2026 ) . In Table 5(c) , we find that λ SD = 0.01 \lambda_{\mathrm{SD}}=0.01 performs best among the evaluated coefficients, while a larger coefficient of 0.1 0.1 achieves comparable performance. Finally, in Table 5(d) , we find that stopping gradients from the action loss to the video backbone improves the success rate from 65.6% → \to 68.8%, suggesting that optimizing future video representations directly for action prediction is not necessarily beneficial.
paragraphs.zh: 自蒸馏的设计选择。 我们分析了 FRED 的若干设计选择：教师噪声水平、用于自蒸馏和动作条件化的特征提取层、自蒸馏损失系数，以及从动作损失到视频扩散主干网络的梯度流动。 在表 5(a) 中，我们发现噪声水平适中的教师输入（τ = 0.25 \tau=0.25）表现最佳，优于干净的未来观测以及受噪声破坏更严重的输入。 我们推测，适度的噪声破坏能为自蒸馏提供更具信息量的目标表征，这与先前的研究观察一致，即扩散模型的表征在中等噪声水平下可能最为有效（Yu et al., 2025；Vélez et al., 2025）。 在表 5(b) 中，我们发现性能在第 18 层达到峰值，而使用更浅或更深的层都会导致性能下降，这与先前在世界自回归模型（WAM）中的发现一致，即视频模型的中间层能为动作条件化提供更有效的表征（Ma et al., 2026）。 在表 5(c) 中，我们发现 λ SD = 0.01 \lambda_{\mathrm{SD}}=0.01 在所评估的系数中表现最佳，而更大的系数 0.1 0.1 也达到了相当的性能。 最后，在表 5(d) 中，我们发现阻断从动作损失到视频主干网络的梯度可以将成功率从 65.6% 提升 \to 68.8%，这表明直接为动作预测而优化未来视频表征并不一定有益。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we have presented FRED, a novel framework for training World Action Models (WAMs) that explicitly learns the future representations used for action generation from a single video denoising step via self-distillation. Our key insight is to view the video diffusion model (VDM) as a future representation generator and explicitly improve these representations by aligning them with self-distillation targets extracted from noisy future observations, while using observation history as additional temporal context. Our experiments show that FRED consistently improves robot control in complex real-world scenarios, including zero-shot environment generalization and human-to-robot skill transfer. We hope our work on the connection between representation learning and WAMs encourages further work toward efficient and generalizable robot foundation models that better leverage large-scale pre-trained video models. We provide more discussion in Appendix F .
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们提出了 FRED，一个用于训练世界动作模型（WAM）的新颖框架，它通过自蒸馏从单步视频去噪中显式学习用于动作生成的未来表征。 我们的核心见解是将视频扩散模型（VDM）视为一个未来表征生成器，并通过将未来表征与从含噪未来观测中提取的自蒸馏目标对齐来显式地改进这些表征，同时利用观测历史作为额外的时间上下文。 我们的实验表明，FRED 在复杂真实世界场景中持续提升机器人控制性能，包括零样本环境泛化和人机技能迁移。 我们希望这项关于表征学习与 WAM 之间联系的工作能够激励更多研究，朝着更高效、更具泛化能力、并能更好地利用大规模预训练视频模型的机器人基础模型迈进。 我们在附录 F 中提供了更多讨论。

paragraphs.en: Implementation Details for Real-world Experiments. For the Franka Research 3 experiments, we use Wan2.2-TI2V-5B and Wan2.1-I2V-14B as the 5B and 14B video diffusion backbones, respectively, while all OpenArm experiments use Wan2.2-TI2V-5B. We condition the video model on 4 historical frames with the current frame, and predict 8 future frames, with a temporal stride of 3. For FRED, we use the same intermediate layer for self-distillation and action conditioning (19th layer for Wan2.2-5B and 25th layer for Wan2.1-14B). Across all experiments, we use γ 1 = 0.1 \gamma_{1}=0.1 , γ 2 = 0.04 \gamma_{2}=0.04 , teacher noise level τ = 0.25 \tau=0.25 , and λ SD = 0.01 \lambda_{\mathrm{SD}}=0.01 . We update the teacher with an exponential moving average (EMA) using the 1 − ( 1 + t ) − 3 / 4 1-(1+t)^{-3/4} warmup decay schedule implemented in Diffusers. We normalize actions and proprioceptive states using Q01-Q99 normalization. We train the Franka 5B and 14B models for 150K and 100K iterations with batch size 128. OpenArm models are trained for 50K iterations; robot-only training uses batch size 32, while robot-human co-training uses 32 robot and 32 human samples per batch. All models are optimized with AdamW and cosine learning rate decay. For the 14B FRED model trained on DROID, we set the video-model learning rate to 10 − 5 10^{-5} , following DreamZero. For all other settings, we use a learning rate of 10 − 4 10^{-4} for both the video model and action decoder.
paragraphs.zh: 真实世界实验的实现细节。 对于 Franka Research 3 实验，我们分别使用 Wan2.2-TI2V-5B 和 Wan2.1-I2V-14B 作为 5B 和 14B 的视频扩散骨干，而所有 OpenArm 实验均使用 Wan2.2-TI2V-5B。 我们让视频模型以 4 个历史帧和当前帧为条件，预测 8 个未来帧，时间步长为 3。 对于 FRED，我们在自蒸馏和动作条件化中使用相同的中间层（Wan2.2-5B 为第 19 层，Wan2.1-14B 为第 25 层）。 在所有实验中，我们使用 γ₁=0.1、γ₂=0.04、教师噪声水平 τ=0.25 以及 λ_SD=0.01。 我们使用 Diffusers 中实现的 1−(1+t)^{-3/4} 预热衰减调度，通过指数移动平均（EMA）更新教师模型。 我们使用 Q01-Q99 归一化对动作和本体感知状态进行归一化。 我们以批量大小 128 分别训练 Franka 5B 和 14B 模型 150K 和 100K 次迭代。 OpenArm 模型训练 50K 次迭代；仅机器人训练使用批量大小 32，而机器人-人类协同训练每批使用 32 个机器人样本和 32 个人类样本。 所有模型均使用 AdamW 和余弦学习率衰减进行优化。 对于在 DROID 上训练的 14B FRED 模型，我们遵循 DreamZero，将视频模型的学习率设为 10^{-5}。 对于所有其他设置，我们对视频模型和动作解码器均使用 10^{-4} 的学习率。

paragraphs.en: For baseline comparisons, we follow the official implementation of each method if it is available. Specifically, for VideoREPA ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , we follow its official implementation with a VideoMAEv2 ViT-B encoder ( Wang et al., 2023 ) to produce the alignment target, modifying only the encoder input to match our input resolution and prediction horizon. paragraphs.en: Hardware Setup. We evaluate models trained on DROID in a new environment without additional training on data from the evaluation environment. For π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} and GR00T N1.7, we follow the official implementations that use the wrist camera and the left exterior camera. The action space consists of relative joint angles (7D) and an absolute gripper opening (1D). For the remaining models, we use both the left and right exterior cameras. paragraphs.en: Evaluation Details. We evaluate four task sets: (a) in-domain easy tasks , (b) in-domain long-horizon tasks , (c) out-of-domain tasks , and (d) object grounding tasks . We consider a task in-domain if its instruction is present in DROID, and out-of-domain otherwise. The object grounding tasks test whether the policy can distinguish objects with similar colors or shapes. We evaluate each task over 12 trials and report the success rates with partial credit ( e . g ., 0.5) for partial task completion ( e . g ., pick only). We limit each trial to 1,500 action steps for long-horizon tasks and 500 action steps for all other tasks (see Figure 6 for visualization of the tasks).
paragraphs.zh: 评估细节。 我们评估四个任务集：(a) 域内简单任务，(b) 域内长时程任务，(c) 域外任务，以及 (d) 物体定位任务。 如果任务的指令出现在 DROID 中，我们认为该任务是域内的，否则是域外的。 物体定位任务测试策略能否区分颜色或形状相似的物体。 我们对每个任务进行 12 次试验，并报告带有部分得分的成功率（例如 0.5），部分得分对应部分任务完成（例如仅完成抓取）。 我们将每次试验限制为：长时程任务 1,500 个动作步，其他所有任务 500 个动作步（任务可视化见图 6）。

paragraphs.en: Hardware Setup. We use the OpenArm humanoid 3 3 3 https://openarm.dev/ , which consists of two 7-DoF arms. Each arm is equipped with a 6-DoF Inspire RH56F1 hand, while the head is mounted on a 2-DoF neck supporting pitch and yaw motions. We use relative joint actions for the arms, absolute actions for the hands, and absolute actions for the neck. A ZED 2i stereo camera is mounted on the neck, and we use its left and right egocentric views as visual inputs in all experiments. For data collection, we teleoperate the two arms using ExoArm-7, a wearable exoskeleton compatible with OpenArm. Finger motions are captured using Manus Pro gloves, which provide fingertip positions that are converted to finger joint angles through inverse kinematics. We visualize the hardware setup in Figure 7 .

paragraphs.en: Training Dataset. For the robot dataset, we collect 553 teleoperated demonstrations on the OpenArm platform, comprising 192K frames. paragraphs.en: We consider vision-language-action models and video diffusion-based models.
paragraphs.zh: 我们考虑视觉-语言-动作模型和基于视频扩散的模型。

paragraphs.en: π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ( Black et al., 2025 ) is a diffusion-based Vision-Language-Action model (VLA) that combines a vision-language backbone with a flow-matching action transformer. It shares self-attention layers between the VLM and the diffusion transformer.
paragraphs.zh: π 0.5 \pi_{0.5}（Black et al., 2025）是一个基于扩散的视觉-语言-动作模型（VLA），它将视觉-语言骨干网络与流匹配动作 Transformer 相结合。 它在 VLM 与扩散 Transformer 之间共享自注意力层。

sents.en: π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ( Black et al., 2025 ) is a diffusion-based Vision-Language-Action model (VLA) that combines a vision-language backbone with a flow-matching action transformer.
sents.zh: π 0.5 \pi_{0.5}（Black et al., 2025）是一个基于扩散的视觉-语言-动作模型（VLA），它将视觉-语言骨干网络与流匹配动作 Transformer 相结合。

sents.en: It shares self-attention layers between the VLM and the diffusion transformer.
sents.zh: 它在 VLM 与扩散 Transformer 之间共享自注意力层。

paragraphs.en: GR00T N1.7 ( NVIDIA, 2026 ) is also a diffusion-based VLA, but it feeds the intermediate hidden states of the VLM into the cross-attention layer of the diffusion transformer.
paragraphs.zh: GR00T N1.7（NVIDIA，2026）同样是一个基于扩散模型的 VLA，但它将 VLM 的中间隐藏状态输入到扩散 Transformer 的交叉注意力层中。

paragraphs.en: DreamZero ( Ye et al., 2026 ) is a World Action Model (WAM) built on a pre-trained video diffusion model that jointly predicts future videos and robot actions through a single backbone.
paragraphs.zh: DreamZero (Ye et al., 2026) 是一种世界动作模型（WAM），它构建在预训练的视频扩散模型之上，通过单一骨干网络联合预测未来视频和机器人动作。

paragraphs.en: DiT4DiT ( Ma et al., 2026 ) is a WAM that uses separate video and action diffusion transformers, where intermediate denoising features from the video transformer condition the action transformer through cross-attention without decoding future frames.
paragraphs.zh: DiT4DiT（Ma et al., 2026）是一种 WAM，它使用分离的视频扩散变换器和动作扩散变换器，其中视频变换器的中间去噪特征通过交叉注意力来调节动作变换器，而无需解码未来帧。

paragraphs.en: Fast-WAM ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) is also a WAM that uses separate video and action diffusion transformers, while using attention masking to prevent action prediction from depending on future video tokens, thereby omitting future video prediction at inference.
paragraphs.zh: Fast-WAM（Yuan et al., 2026）同样是一种使用分离的视频与动作扩散 transformer 的 WAM，同时利用注意力掩码防止动作预测依赖于未来的视频 token，从而在推理时省略对未来视频的预测。

paragraphs.en: AGRA ( Qiu et al., 2026 ) extends a separate video-action architecture with an action-grounded representation alignment objective that aligns intermediate video diffusion features with spatially coherent features from a frozen visual encoder, while jointly updating the video backbone with the robot action objective.
paragraphs.zh: AGRA（Qiu et al., 2026）在独立的视频-动作架构基础上扩展了一个动作锚定的表征对齐目标，将中间视频扩散特征与来自冻结视觉编码器的空间一致特征进行对齐，同时结合机器人动作目标联合更新视频主干网络。

paragraphs.en: Attentive Probe Architecture. Following recent self-supervised learning literature, we use a lightweight attentive probe on top of the frozen video representations ( Bardes et al., 2024 ; Assran et al., 2025 ) to evaluate the quality of video representations. Specifically, it consists of a single learnable query token cross-attending to the video tokens through a 12-head cross-attention block, followed by an MLP and a linear classifier for 15-way motion primitive classification.
paragraphs.zh: 注意力探测架构。 遵循近期的自监督学习文献，我们在冻结的视频表示之上使用一个轻量级的注意力探测（ Bardes et al., 2024 ； Assran et al., 2025 ）来评估视频表示的质量。 具体而言，它由单个可学习的查询 token 组成，通过一个 12 头交叉注意力模块对视频 token 进行交叉注意，其后接一个 MLP 和一个用于 15 类运动基元分类的线性分类器。

paragraphs.en: Attentive Probe Training and Evaluation. We train the attentive probe using 300 demonstrations per task used for policy training on RoboCasa Kitchen ( Nasiriany et al., 2024 ) , and evaluate it on 50 newly generated demonstrations per task. We extract the intermediate future-token representations from layer 18 of the frozen video backbone and train the probe for 10 epochs with the AdamW optimizer using a batch size of 128, a learning rate of 10 − 3 10^{-3} , and weight decay of 0.05. We report the best validation top-1 accuracy over the 10 epochs.
paragraphs.zh: 注意力探针的训练与评估。 我们使用用于在 RoboCasa Kitchen（Nasiriany et al., 2024）上进行策略训练的每任务 300 条演示来训练注意力探针，并在每任务新生成的 50 条演示上进行评估。 我们从冻结的视频骨干网络的第 18 层提取中间的未来 token 表示，并使用 AdamW 优化器训练探针 10 个 epoch，批量大小为 128，学习率为 10 − 3 10^{-3}，权重衰减为 0.05。 我们报告 10 个 epoch 中最佳的验证集 top-1 准确率。

paragraphs.en: To measure the similarity between representation spaces, we use Centered Kernel Nearest-Neighbor Alignment (CKNNA; Huh et al. 2024 ), a relaxed variant of Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA; Kornblith et al. 2019 ). We compute CKNNA on 4,096 clips randomly sampled from the validation set of attentive probing analysis. For each WAM checkpoint, we extract the intermediate future-token representations from layer 18 of the video backbone and mean-pool the 192 future-frame tokens to obtain a clip-level representation. We use representations extracted from clean future observations ( τ = 0.0 \tau=0.0 ) by the Base WAM ( i . e ., DiT4DiT) trained at 100K iterations as a fixed reference, and measure their alignment with representations obtained from noise ( τ = 1.0 \tau=1.0 ) at each checkpoint of the Base WAM and FRED from 20K to 100K iterations.
paragraphs.zh: 为了度量表示空间之间的相似性，我们采用中心化核最近邻对齐（CKNNA；Huh et al. 2024），它是中心化核对齐（CKA；Kornblith et al. 2019）的一种宽松变体。 我们从注意力探测分析（attentive probing）的验证集中随机抽取 4,096 个片段来计算 CKNNA。 对于每个 WAM 检查点，我们从视频骨干网络的第 18 层提取中间的未来 token 表示，并对 192 个未来帧 token 进行均值池化，以得到片段级表示。 我们使用由在 100K 次迭代处训练的基础 WAM（即 DiT4DiT）从干净的未来观测（τ = 0.0 \tau=0.0）中提取的表示作为固定参考，并度量其与基础 WAM 和 FRED 从 20K 到 100K 次迭代的每个检查点处由噪声（τ = 1.0 \tau=1.0）得到的表示之间的对齐程度。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate one-step video generation quality using Fréchet Video Distance (FVD; Unterthiner et al. 2018 ) between 2,048 generated videos and 2,048 randomly sampled clips from the RoboCasa Kitchen training set ( Nasiriany et al., 2024 ) . For DMD2 ( Yin et al., 2024 ) , we train a one-step student in two stages. First, we fine-tune the Wan2.2-TI2V-5B model ( Wan et al., 2025 ) on RoboCasa Kitchen ( Nasiriany et al., 2024 ) for 100K iterations with a global batch size of 64. We then distill the fine-tuned model’s EMA teacher into a one-step student, following the NVIDIA FastGen implementation ( Nie et al., 2026 ) , for 5K iterations with a global batch size of 16, without classifier-free guidance ( Ho & Salimans, 2022 ) and with a GAN loss weight of 0.1.

paragraphs.en: A potential limitation of FRED is its reliance on the language understanding capabilities of the underlying video diffusion backbone, as our training objective focuses on future representation learning and does not provide additional supervision for language grounding. As shown in Table 2(b) , without human-video co-training, FRED achieves 0% instruction-following performance on the human skill transfer tasks, while pre-trained VLA baselines retain some instruction-following ability. Co-training with human videos substantially improves this performance, suggesting that stronger language grounding may further benefit generalization to unseen instructions. Future work could combine the spatiotemporal priors of video diffusion models with the stronger language grounding of pre-trained vision-language models.
paragraphs.zh: FRED 的一个潜在局限在于它依赖于底层视频扩散主干网络的语言理解能力，因为我们的训练目标是未来表征学习，并未为语言对齐提供额外的监督。 如表 2(b) 所示，在没有人类视频协同训练的情况下，FRED 在人类技能迁移任务上的指令遵循性能为 0%，而预训练的 VLA 基线仍保留了一定的指令遵循能力。 与人类视频协同训练显著提升了这一性能，这表明更强的语言对齐能力可能进一步有利于对未见指令的泛化。 未来的工作可以将视频扩散模型的时空先验与预训练视觉-语言模型更强的语言对齐能力相结合。

paragraphs.en: Another limitation is that human-to-robot transfer in FRED remains implicit: human and robot videos jointly train the video model, but we do not explicitly learn correspondences between their representations across embodiments. Although human-video co-training substantially improves instruction following, task success remains moderate. Future work could explore explicit cross-embodiment representation learning to better transfer human-demonstrated skills to robot control.
paragraphs.zh: 另一个局限是，FRED 中的人到机器人迁移仍然是隐式的：人类视频和机器人视频共同训练视频模型，但我们并未显式学习它们在不同本体之间的表征对应关系。 尽管人类视频协同训练显著提升了指令遵循能力，任务成功率仍然中等。 未来的工作可以探索显式的跨本体表征学习，以更好地将人类演示的技能迁移到机器人控制中。

paragraphs.en: To further verify the effectiveness of our method, we additionally compare FRED with state-of-the-art robot foundation models on the RoboCasa Kitchen benchmark. As shown in Table 13 , we find that FRED achieves the highest average success rate, demonstrating that our method not only exhibits strong generalization and transferability in real-world manipulation scenarios but also has the potential to achieve leading simulation benchmark performance when sufficient computational resources are available. We note that these results differ from those in Table 4 because we adjust the training configurations to be comparable to those of competing VLAs and WAMs. Specifically, we train FRED with a global batch size of 256 for 100K iterations, keeping all other hyperparameters unchanged, while the reported baseline results are taken from their original papers or official code repositories.
paragraphs.zh: 为了进一步验证我们方法的有效性，我们还在 RoboCasa Kitchen 基准上将 FRED 与最先进的机器人基础模型进行了比较。 如表 13 所示，我们发现 FRED 取得了最高的平均成功率，这表明我们的方法不仅在真实世界操作场景中表现出强大的泛化性和可迁移性，而且在拥有足够计算资源时有潜力取得领先的仿真基准性能。 我们注意到，这些结果与表 4 中的结果不同，因为我们调整了训练配置，使其与竞争的 VLA 和 WAM 的训练配置相当。 具体而言，我们以全局批大小 256 训练 FRED 进行 10 万次迭代，其余所有超参数保持不变，而所报告的基线结果取自其原始论文或官方代码仓库。

sents.zh: 如表 13 所示，我们发现 FRED 取得了最高的平均成功率，这表明我们的方法不仅在真实世界操作场景中表现出强大的泛化性和可迁移性，而且在拥有足够计算资源时有潜力取得领先的仿真基准性能。

sents.en: We note that these results differ from those in Table 4 because we adjust the training configurations to be comparable to those of competing VLAs and WAMs.
sents.zh: 我们注意到，这些结果与表 4 中的结果不同，因为我们调整了训练配置，使其与竞争的 VLA 和 WAM 的训练配置相当。

sents.en: Specifically, we train FRED with a global batch size of 256 for 100K iterations, keeping all other hyperparameters unchanged, while the reported baseline results are taken from their original papers or official code repositories.
